subject: AI & Agents
title: Social Media Feeds: The AI Curator
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Social Media Feeds: The AI Curator.

hook.text: You open Instagram for one minute. Thirty minutes later you're still scrolling. That's by design.

buildup.text: Feed algorithms rank content by predicted engagement — likes, comments, shares, watch time.

discovery.text: AI models learn that outrage and surprise get the most engagement. So they promote both.

twist.text: The algorithm isn't evil — it optimizes for the metric it was given. The metric was wrong.

climax.text: Platforms now face pressure to optimize for well-being, not just engagement.

punchline.text: The feed isn't curated for you. It's curated against your willpower.

quiz.question: What do social media algorithms primarily optimize for?
options: User engagement metrics like likes, comments, and watch time

details.summary: Social media algorithms curate your feed by predicting which posts will maximize your engagement. AI decides what you see based on your interactions, social connections, and content characteristics.
details.whyItMatters: Algorithm-curated feeds shape public opinion, political views, and mental health. Understanding how they work empowers users to make intentional choices about their media consumption.
takeaways: Algorithms optimize feeds for engagement, not necessarily quality
Your interactions train the AI to show more similar content
Feed curation contributes to filter bubbles and polarization

faq.question: How do social media algorithms decide what you see?
faq.answer: They score every potential post based on predicted engagement: likelihood of likes, comments, shares, and time spent viewing. Posts with the highest predicted scores appear at the top of your feed.

faq.question: Can you control what the algorithm shows you?
faq.answer: Partially. You can mute topics, unfollow accounts, and use chronological feed options where available. But platforms default to algorithmic feeds because they maximize time spent on the app.
